subject: EU/APAC SI ingress & trust playbook — alignment and MAP
messages:
From: Sven Mueller <sven.mueller@atlantic-systems.de>

Subject: Re: EU/APAC SI ingress & trust playbook — initial ask

Hi all,

Thanks again for taking this on. Pacific Consulting and Atlantic Systems are partnering to run several private deployments for EU and APAC customers where the partner will manage the local edge/HSM layer and handle first-line on-site ops. Before we start pilot installs we need to align on a short, prescriptive "ingress & trust" checklist that covers:

- data ingress patterns (direct to Redwood vs partner-managed gateway)
- encryption in transit and at rest (who holds keys, KMS/HSM detail)
- audit log provenance (what logs partner must forward vs Redwood retained)
- proof-of-residency artifact requirements (signed attestations, logging TTLs)

Attached is a rough trust framework we've sketched (SI_Trust_Framework_v1.pdf). Can you confirm the minimum evidence Redwood will accept to classify a deployment as "partner-managed, local-residency-compliant"? Also: we prefer a single mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones rather than ad hoc emails.

Proposed attendees for a 60-min sync: olga (platform lead), rafael (infra), laura (privacy), myself, Mei Tan (PacCon lead), and one legal contact from each side.

Best,
Sven
Partner Engagement Lead
Atlantic Systems

Subject: Re: EU/APAC SI ingress & trust playbook — initial ask

Sven / Mei,

Appreciate the clarity. High level answers up front:

1) Minimum evidence to classify "partner-managed, local-residency-compliant":
   - Signed partner attestation (delegated custodianship scope)
   - KMS/HSM diagram showing key custody and rotation (partner vs customer vs Redwood)
   - Data flow map with egress controls and retention TTLs (PNG preferred, we annotated yours)
   - Audit log forwarding contract (S3/LogPush + signed retention policy)

2) We can accept partner-managed ingress under two models: (A) partner gateway routes to Redwood-hosted model endpoint but partner never persists raw customer data; (B) partner-hosted enclave where Redwood provides model artifacts and model serving runs on partner infra under a narrow SLA. Each model has different evidence needs (we list those in the attached SOW draft).

3) MAP: agree on milestones — compliance evidence, staging install, canary ingest test, privacy review sign-off, production cutover. I'll draft a MAP after we sync.

Proposed times for 60-min sync next week (I blocked tentative slots):
- Tue 2027-04-12 09:00-10:00 PDT
- Wed 2027-04-13 15:00-16:00 PDT

Rafael / Laura: please review the trust framework and SOW and add redlines inline; this will prevent long follow-up loops.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Thanks Olga. Quick clarifications from the SI side before the call:

- For APAC pilots, customers require HSM-backed key custody in-country. Is Redwood able to support partner-managed HSM (partner provides HSM and Redwood accepts signed key escrow policy)?
- On log retention: customers often require logs held for 7 years for certain regulated verticals in APAC — can Redwood accept a forward-and-store model where partner pushes audit logs into our secured bucket but the partner keeps a copy locally?

Looping in LegalOps (legal@globalsec.com) to confirm whether a standardized attestation template is acceptable or if customers will need bespoke language.

We can take the Tue 4/12 slot. I'll prepare a short deck of the SI operating model to share before the call.

Cheers,
Mei
Principal, Pacific Consulting

Subject: Re: EU/APAC SI ingress & trust playbook — post-call notes

Team — thanks for a productive sync. Notes from my side (condensed):

- HSM/key custody: Redwood will accept partner-managed HSM where partner is the KMS primary, subject to:
  * annual security attestation + quarterly key custody logs delivered to Redwood
  * policy that allows Redwood to rotate or revoke keys in emergency (we'll include this in the SOW)
- Audit logs: Redwood can accept partner-forwarded logs into a segregated S3 bucket under Redwood control; partner copy is permitted for local compliance but Redwood must be able to provide log provenance for audits.
- Proof-of-residency: we agreed on three acceptable artifacts — signed partner attestation, network egress test report (a tool-run during canary), and signed installation manifest with geo-tags.
- MAP milestones (owner):
  * 1) Evidence packet submitted (Partner) — due 2027-04-19
  * 2) Staging install & canary ingest test (Redwood + Partner) — window 2027-04-26 to 2027-05-03
  * 3) Privacy review sign-off (Laura) — due 2027-05-07
  * 4) Production cutover (Joint) — target 2027-05-20

Action items:
- Olga: upload redlined SOW and MAP to Confluence page (please link).
- Rafael: prepare a short canary test script template and retention policy excerpt.
- Partner: deliver evidence packet (attestation + KMS diagram + data flow map) by 4/19.

I'll draft privacy sign-off checklist and post to the Confluence link after review.

Laura Bennett
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
